title: Indo-European
blurb: Every language here descends from a single ancestor spoken around 5,000 years ago. Cognates are everywhere once you start looking — but the further apart the branches, the better they hide.

title: East & Southeast Asia
blurb: Unrelated families sharing a neighbourhood — and centuries of borrowed vocabulary. Watch for the words Chinese lent to everyone, and the ones Europe lent for bread.

title: South Asia, Middle East & North Africa
blurb: Two very different halves. In South Asia, Indo-Aryan and Dravidian languages have traded words for millennia; across the Middle East and North Africa, Semitic roots and Arabic loans run through everything. Three classical languages sit in here too — Sanskrit, Syriac and Ge'ez — so you can watch the modern words drift off their ancestors.

title: The grand tour
blurb: The wide net: Bantu and Volta-Niger from Africa, Austronesian from across the Pacific, and an isolate related to nothing else on earth. Expect to guess more than you know.
